call_points.text: Management says Q1FY27 results are in line with annual estimates and it is on track for the full year across all financial parameters.
Segment growth guidance: basmati 10-12%, RTH 15-20%, organic 10-12%.
US RTH facility expected to become operational this quarter, which management says will accelerate segment growth.
No capex planned for the newly opened Australia entity; only a small equity infusion so far.
International business was 71% of consolidated revenue; North America grew 49% on a normalized basis.
Organic gross margin fell to 33% from 35% last year, and CIF-to-C&I shipment terms shifted cost into gross margin.
Rice inventory 3,46,000 tonnes at ₹56/kg average and paddy 1,64,000 tonnes at ₹38/kg, enough for next year's branded demand.
Middle East freight rose from $200 to $4,000 a container and could not be passed on, hurting Europe, UK and Middle East margins.
US duty refunds partly received but no income booked yet; company is in talks with customers.
Management expects continued double-digit revenue growth supported by global demand and new product launches.
Ready-to-heat capacity constraints will be resolved with enhanced capacities operational from Q2 FY27.
Ready-to-Heat capacity constraints limited FY26 growth; new capacity coming online in Q2FY27.
Q4 EBITDA was hit by one-time US tariff costs and a strategic shift in brand spending.

operating_notes.text: The Group operates as a single primary reportable segment, manufacturing, trading and marketing of rice, per Ind AS 108.
The consolidated results include the holding company, twenty one subsidiaries, two joint ventures and five associates.

LT Foods Americas Inc. acquired the remaining 49% of Golden Star Trading Inc. for USD 15 million (₹128.50 Cr) on May 22, 2025, making it a wholly owned subsidiary, with a ₹9.34 Cr remeasurement gain booked in other income.
FY26: Working capital days reduced to 176 from 196 in FY25.
FY26: Net Debt / EBITDA stood at 0.60x compared to 0.56x in FY25.
FY26: Royal brand commands over 60% Basmati rice import share in North America.
FY26 working capital days improved to 176 days from 196 days.
Q1FY27 rice inventory was 3,46,000 tonnes at an average ₹56/kg and paddy 1,64,000 tonnes at ₹38/kg, sufficient for the next year's branded demand.
US basmati import share is more than 60%; India market share was 23.1% with household penetration of 64.4 lakh households.
Logistics cost was 4.7% of revenue in Q1FY27; Middle East freight rose from $200 to $4,000 a container.
Launched 'Har Din Baney Perfect' campaign for DAAWAT Rozana featuring Chef Ranveer Brar to drive branded Basmati penetration.
Nature Bio Foods acquired controlling stake in Leev.nu B.V. taking its share to 70.75% for €1.735 million.
International revenue accounts for 71% of H1 FY27 total revenue.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,906.7 Cr (+30.4% YoY), net profit ₹135.67 Cr (-15.5% YoY).
LT Foods reported FY26 revenue growth of 19% to ₹11,023 Cr, though Q4 profit was impacted by one-time US tariff costs and higher brand investments.
LT Foods reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹11,023 Cr (+26% YoY) and PAT of ₹625 Cr, driven by strong global demand and premiumisation.
Wholly owned subsidiary KAMEDA LT FOODS (INDIA) PRIVATE LIMITED changed name to KLT FOODS (INDIA) PRIVATE LIMITED effective October 14, 2026.
LT Foods launched a new brand campaign for DAAWAT Rozana featuring Chef Ranveer Brar on October 26, 2026.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,234.14 Cr, net profit ₹180.2 Cr (+10.0% YoY).
LT Foods reported H1 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹6,414 Cr and PAT of ₹364 Cr, supported by strong international expansion and improved working capital.
